A user finds searching HN through Google gives better results than the Algolia-powered HN search. Searching "ml" on Algolia returned years-old, less relevant results, while Google surfaced more recent threads.
A user much prefers Algolia over Google for searching HN. They find the customization very helpful: search by user or by type, and order stories by popularity or date.
A user says Algolia doesn't seem great for HN. Lately the search sometimes fails to load results or is quite slow compared to Google Search. Another user said they have hit the same problem.

Algolia's DocSearch program for open source projects is really great; the Jekyll docs' instant results usually find just what you want. Only complaint: wants a plug-and-play solution deployable for private internal documentation sites.

A user praises Algolia's analytics. You can tie a search query to a purchase and analyze it further, which lets you measure business value from actual search queries without exceptional engineering talent.

A former customer says Algolia is easy to use and set up, like pre-docker Heroku. They switched to Elasticsearch over price and the closed-source license. In their view Algolia is great to start with but doesn't make sense at scale, since large indexes are too expensive.
A team moved to Algolia mainly for speed, saying Elasticsearch and Solr could not compete.

A user who configured Algolia for their docs site is really happy with the service and the ease of implementation. However, because their docs can take a few seconds to load, the crawler sometimes times out and misses content.

A user running Algolia on a side project is very impressed with the developer experience. They call the React InstantSearch plugin great and easy to add, and also praise the documentation and admin UI.

A team A/B testing Typesense and Algolia says the pricing difference alone almost makes them skip the test and choose Typesense. They call Algolia's price-per-search model a little ridiculous for UIs with live search.
A user calls InstantSearch one of Algolia's strongest features, with support for vanilla JS, React, Vue, Angular, iOS and Android, and hopes alternatives reach that level of support.

A user who has used Algolia for small sites and large enterprise clients says no SaaS business has executed such a smooth onboarding and retention ecosystem. They always felt they got way more than they paid for.
A user says that if you've tried installing Elasticsearch and then switched to Algolia, you'll understand how great a product it is.
A user finds the HN search performs quite poorly. It seems to do fuzzy matching and weird relevance ranking rather than the full-index text search they want.

A user uses Algolia's free version for Facebook open source sites like React, GraphQL and Yarn. Setup is just a JS file and an input, with zero maintenance, no downtime and no API changes, and users get fast, quality search.

A user built search with Algolia, React Native and Firebase over users' names, bios, phones and more. Linking the two took a single Firebase cloud function after importing data with a simple node script. They say the typo tolerance alone makes Algolia the best third-party search service.

On Adafruit, which the user believes runs on Algolia, results start strong but quickly fall off into partial gibberish. Searching "lipo" mixed relevant items with random microcontrollers, LEDs and motors by the end of page 1. The user guesses this is the implementation and notes category refinement helps.

A team searching about 1.5M US nonprofits finds Algolia blazing fast, super customizable and backed by helpful support. It handles typos, alternate names, EINs and locations, with per-user customization. Their only complaint is that pricing is a bit steep, though setting up Elasticsearch comparably would take far more time.

A user says it's easy to exceed Algolia's record limits because every 'sort by' option needs a duplicate replica index. Adding date ascending/descending and price sorts turned 30K records into 150K, which pushed them toward building something custom.

A user misses the old HN search. The Algolia-based one has nice features but lacks basic search commands like OR queries (e.g. "ai OR artificial intelligence"). Another user wishes fuzzy matching could be turned off in some cases.
